name: Hereditary Fanconi Syndrome

criteria.description: Evidence of generalized proximal tubular dysfunction including aminoaciduria, glycosuria, and phosphaturia
Persistent hypophosphatemia due to renal phosphate wasting
Presence of proximal (type 2) renal tubular acidosis
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with proximal tubule function

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of generalized proximal tubular dysfunction with at least two major criteria (aminoaciduria, glycosuria, phosphaturia) plus hypophosphatemia and renal tubular acidosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is supported by genetic testing and family history but primarily based on biochemical and clinical findings.

pathognomonic.notes: Excretion of multiple amino acids in urine
Glucose in urine despite normal blood glucose levels
Excess phosphate loss in urine leading to low serum phosphate
searchTerms: phosphate loss in urine with low blood phosphate
low phosphate levels due to kidney loss

common.notes: Increased urine output due to impaired tubular reabsorption
Secondary to polyuria and electrolyte loss
Due to electrolyte imbalances, especially hypophosphatemia
Resulting from chronic electrolyte and nutrient loss
Proximal renal tubular acidosis causing acid-base imbalance

occasional.notes: Bone disease secondary to phosphate wasting
searchTerms: bone deformities from vitamin D deficiency

occasional.notes: Low serum potassium due to renal losses
Generalized tiredness related to electrolyte disturbances
Low serum uric acid due to renal tubular loss

rare.notes: Low serum magnesium due to renal wasting
Rare impairment of renal concentrating ability
searchTerms: excessive urination due to kidney issue

laboratory: Generalized aminoaciduria on urine amino acid analysis
Proximal (type 2) renal tubular acidosis with metabolic acidosis
imaging: Radiographic evidence of rickets or osteomalacia
Nephrocalcinosis on renal ultrasound or CT
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes affecting proximal tubular function (e.g., SLC34A1, EHHADH, or others depending on subtype)
other: Family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance
Response to phosphate and bicarbonate supplementation

distinguishingFeatures: History of exposure to toxins, drugs, or heavy metals
Potential reversibility after removal of offending agent
Isolated proximal renal tubular acidosis without generalized aminoaciduria

references: Gahl WA, Thoene JG, Schneider JA. Cystinosis. N Engl J Med. 2002;347(2):111-121.
Scheinman SJ. Fanconi syndrome and other proximal renal tubular disorders. Pediatr Nephrol. 2002;17(11):959-969.
